title: Homeowner Identity Exposure During Account Registration
description: During account registration, the homeowner's personally identifiable information (PII) is transmitted to the Home Hub, creating a risk that this identity information could be exposed or misused.
assumptions: The registration process collects and transmits PII to the Home Hub system.

title: Linkability of Camera/Sensor Data to Homeowner Identity
description: Data collected from enrolled cameras and sensors can be linked to the homeowner's registered account, potentially enabling profiling or tracking of the homeowner's activities and habits.
assumptions: Camera and sensor data is associated with the homeowner's account identity.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Home Surveillance Data
description: Video and sensor data captured by enrolled devices could be disclosed to unauthorized third parties through system vulnerabilities, insider threats, or improper access controls.
assumptions: The Home Hub system may have vulnerabilities or inadequate access controls.

title: Identity Usurpation During Device Enrollment
description: An attacker could potentially impersonate the homeowner to enroll unauthorized cameras or sensors on the Home Hub, gaining access to the home's surveillance system.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms during device enrollment may be weak or bypassable.

title: Guest Access Linked to Identity
description: The guest user's temporary access code entry could be linked to their identity through system logs, potentially revealing who accessed the home and when.
assumptions: System maintains logs of access code entries with user identification

title: Access Code Disclosure via Logging
description: The Home Hub may log the temporary access code, creating a risk of disclosure to unauthorized parties through system access, backups, or data breaches.
assumptions: Access codes are stored or logged by the Home Hub system

title: Unauthorized Code Sharing Enables Access
description: The temporary access code could be shared with unauthorized individuals, allowing them to gain entry to the home through the Home Hub.
assumptions: Guest may share the code with others, or code could be intercepted

title: Disclosure of household activity patterns
description: The local event log containing motion/door/sensor events could reveal sensitive information about household routines, presence patterns, and activities, potentially exposing when occupants are home or away.

title: Linkability of events to individuals
description: Events in the local event log could be linked to specific individuals or activities, potentially revealing associations between people and their movements or actions within the home.

title: Tampering with event log integrity
description: An attacker with physical or digital access to the local event log could modify, delete, or inject false events, compromising the authenticity and reliability of the recorded data.

title: Identification of individuals from event metadata
description: If the event log contains metadata such as timestamps, device IDs, or contextual information, individuals could be identified from the recorded events even without explicit personal data.
uncertainty_note: Uncertainty on whether metadata is actually stored in the event log

title: Identification of individuals in video footage
description: Video clips captured by the Home Hub camera may contain identifiable information about individuals (residents, visitors, passersby), enabling identification without consent.
assumptions: Video footage is clear enough to identify faces or distinguishing features

title: Linkability of video data to other data sources
description: Video clips uploaded to cloud storage could be linked to other data sources (e.g., metadata, timestamps, device identifiers) creating a comprehensive surveillance profile.
assumptions: Metadata or device identifiers are transmitted with video uploads

title: Unauthorized disclosure of video data
description: Cloud video storage may be accessed by unauthorized parties through security breaches, insider threats, or inadequate access controls, leading to privacy violations.
assumptions: Cloud storage provider has security vulnerabilities or insufficient access controls

title: Tampering with video footage
description: Video clips stored in the cloud could be modified, deleted, or altered by unauthorized actors, compromising data integrity and evidence value.
assumptions: Cloud storage lacks integrity protection mechanisms

title: Unauthorized access to Home Hub
description: Attackers could gain unauthorized access to the Home Hub device, potentially intercepting or manipulating video uploads before they reach cloud storage.
assumptions: Home Hub has weak authentication or is physically accessible to attackers

title: Non-compliance with privacy regulations
description: Video surveillance data collection and storage may violate GDPR, CCPA, or other privacy regulations regarding consent, data minimization, and retention policies.
assumptions: Data processing activities are not properly documented or consented to

title: Linkability of Motion Alerts to Specific Users
description: Motion alerts transmitted from the Home Hub could be linked to specific household members or devices, potentially revealing occupancy patterns and user behavior.
assumptions: The system does not adequately anonymize or aggregate motion data before transmission.

title: Identifiability of Occupants via Motion Patterns
description: Real-time motion alerts could reveal which individuals are present in the home, their movement patterns, and potentially their routines, making occupants identifiable even without explicit identification.
assumptions: Motion data is transmitted in real-time without sufficient obfuscation or aggregation.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Motion Data
description: The Mobile App Backend could be compromised or accessed by unauthorized parties, leading to disclosure of sensitive motion alert information about household occupants.
assumptions: The backend lacks adequate access controls or encryption for motion data.

title: Excessive Data Collection of Motion Alerts
description: The system may collect more motion data than necessary for the intended purpose (e.g., security notifications), potentially violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: The data retention and collection policies are not aligned with privacy-by-design principles.

title: Unauthorized interception of motion notification
description: Motion-detected notification transmitted from backend to homeowner's phone could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transmission, revealing that motion was detected at the homeowner's location.
assumptions: Transmission channel is not fully encrypted or authentication is weak

title: Linkability of motion events to homeowner profile
description: Motion-detected notifications could be linked to other data about the homeowner's activities, location patterns, or behavior, creating a comprehensive profile of their daily routines.
assumptions: Multiple data sources exist that can be correlated with motion detection events

title: Excessive data in motion notification
description: Notification may contain more information than necessary (e.g., timestamp precision, location details, camera feed) that could reveal unnecessary details about the homeowner's activities.
assumptions: Notification includes metadata beyond simple alert
uncertainty_note: Depends on actual notification payload design

title: Unauthorized notification access via compromised device
description: Homeowner's device could be compromised, allowing unauthorized parties to access motion-detected notifications and infer presence or activity at the property.
assumptions: Homeowner's device has security vulnerabilities or malware

title: Linkability of Aggregated Analytics
description: Aggregated device-usage analytics shared with cloud vendor may be linkable to specific users or devices through cross-referencing with other data sources, enabling potential re-identification.
assumptions: Vendor has access to additional data sources that could be correlated with the analytics data.

title: Unauthorized Data Disclosure to Third Parties
description: Cloud analytics vendor may share or sell the aggregated analytics data to unauthorized third parties, violating user privacy expectations and data sharing agreements.
assumptions: Vendor has insufficient contractual or technical controls to prevent unauthorized data sharing.

title: Inference of User Behavior Patterns
description: Even aggregated analytics may reveal sensitive user behavior patterns, preferences, or habits that could be inferred and potentially misused.
assumptions: Analytics data contains sufficient detail to enable pattern inference about user groups or individuals.

title: Data Integrity Compromise During Storage
description: Cloud analytics vendor may alter, corrupt, or tamper with the aggregated analytics data during storage or processing, compromising data integrity.
assumptions: Vendor's security controls for data integrity are insufficient or not properly implemented.

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance with Data Protection Laws
description: Sharing aggregated analytics with external vendor may violate GDPR, CCPA, or other privacy regulations if proper consent, data minimization, or purpose limitation principles are not followed.
assumptions: Data sharing practices do not fully comply with applicable privacy regulations.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Video Content During Transmission
description: Video clip data transmitted from cloud storage to mobile app backend could be intercepted by unauthorized parties, leading to privacy violations.
assumptions: Transmission channel is not fully encrypted or authentication is weak

title: Video Content Tampering During Transmission
description: Video clip data could be modified or corrupted during transmission from cloud storage to mobile app backend, compromising data integrity.
assumptions: Transmission channel lacks integrity verification mechanisms

title: Video Content Reveals Homeowner Identity and Location
description: Video content retrieved by mobile app backend could reveal the identity, location, or activities of the homeowner, leading to identification risks.
assumptions: Video contains identifiable visual information about the homeowner or their property

title: Video Data Linked to Other Personal Information
description: Video clip data could be linked to other personal data about the homeowner (e.g., name, address, contact info) through metadata or cross-referencing, increasing identifiability.
assumptions: Video metadata or associated data contains linking information

title: Unauthorized Access to Video Playback
description: Mobile app backend could be accessed by unauthorized users who impersonate the homeowner, allowing them to view video content they should not access.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms are weak or compromised
